claims.text: Adding 1 at.% Y to an untreated refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The 1 at.% Y addition will produce a protective Y2O3 oxide layer.
The resulting Y2O3 layer will be dense.
The resulting Y2O3 layer will adhere to the alloy.
The resulting Y2O3 layer will be thermally stable under the stated exposure conditions.
The Y2O3 layer will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion through the Y2O3 layer will reduce the alloy's oxidation rate.
The untreated alloy has an oxidation rate of 10 mg/cm^2/h under the stated conditions.
The Y-treated alloy will have an oxidation rate of 7 mg/cm^2/h under the stated conditions.
The Y addition will reduce oxidation rate by 30% relative to the untreated alloy.
The predicted improvement applies at 1000°C in air at 1 atm and 50% relative humidity after 100 hours of exposure.

contradictions.description: The quantitative hypothesis predicts a 30% reduction, but the falsification rule only requires a 5% reduction to avoid falsification. Thus, outcomes substantially below the stated 30% prediction could be treated as consistent with the hypothesis.
